Development of tolerance to gluten seems possible in some adult patients with celiac disease. While further follow-up may show whether this tolerance is permanent or only a long-term return to latency, research suggests that genetic characteristics, particularly those associated with HLA genotypes such as DQ2 or DQ8, may play a role in the development of gluten tolerance. This information can help distinguish between patients who require lifelong treatment for celiac disease and those who may experience a more temporary resolution.

It is essential to note that some adult patients with celiac disease have developed tolerance to gluten over time, but this does not necessarily mean they are no longer at risk for developing the disease again. Further study is needed to fully understand the mechanisms behind gluten tolerance development in adult patients with celiac disease.
